title: Threshold-sized deterministic BSGS with padded affine batches and paid routing

claims.statement: For the unchanged uniform full-production secp256k1 ECDLP input Q=[x]P, the classical deterministic algorithm in proof.md recovers the canonical x with probability exactly m^2/r >= 39/100, for m=ceil(sqrt(ceil(39r/100))). Its complete cold work, including preprocessing, padded batches, all failures, native-limb arithmetic, routing at both endpoints, sorting, lookup, verification and output, is at most 2^(545/4) target-group-operation equivalents using only the protected C=1000 normalization. Preprocessing is included and bounded by the same ceiling. Peak aggregate storage is below 2^136 bytes; external nonuniform advice is zero bytes (reported log2(max(1,bytes))=0). No statistical or random-walk heuristic is used. This is an analytic construction with explicit instruction and distributed-memory assumptions, not a production execution, native instruction measurement, practical attack, novelty claim or human qualification.

experiments.purpose: Check exact production ledger/coverage inequalities, exhaust a 199-point toy curve, exercise interleaved batches and partial lanes, test small grids over actual secp256k1 and field/counter boundaries. Does not measure production instructions or execute the production search.
